subject: ACME - endorsement sequencing & final COI handback
body:
---Original Message---
From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@harborbrokers.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: ACME - endorsement language & COI timing

Hi Sofia,

Quick follow-up from ACME's broker: ACME is ready to move to signature on the order form but their procurement team is asking for confirmation on two things before countersignature: (1) a certificate of insurance naming them as Additional Insured with the endorsement, and (2) whether Redwood will provide a primary/non-contributing endorsement or if the standard COI + carrier letter will suffice.

Their timeline is tight — they want COI/endorsement confirmation prior to countersignature so they can close finance on Friday. Attached is what their procurement team sent as "acceptable language." I can push to get the issuer to provide an insurer-signed endorsement but need confirmation from your risk/legal on acceptability (naming, waivers, primary language).

Attachment: acme_acceptable_endorsement.txt (text stub)

Can you advise?

Thanks,
Evan
Harbor Brokers

---Reply---
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 09:35:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: ACME - endorsement language & COI timing

Kimberly / Jonas — forwarding Evan's note. ACME asks for an AI endorsement plus clarity on primary/non-contrib. They want confirmation pre-countersignature.

Questions for legal/risk:
- Are we okay with the proposed naming: "ACME Technologies, its subsidiaries and affiliates, and their officers, directors, employees and agents"? We typically prefer to limit to the customer entity + affiliates on order forms.
- Do we require an insurer-issued ISO CG 2011 04/13 or will an insurer-letter of scope + COI be accepted for this deal?
- Any objections to providing primary & non-contrib wording for this counterparty (ACME)? If risk needs a carve, what is the exact wording we should require?

Timeline: ACME is pushing for a certificate or endorsement confirmation before countersign on Friday (2028-08-25). Evan says broker can get insurer to issue endorsement but needs the exact spec.

I'll coordinate.

Sofia Ivanova
Senior Manager, Risk & Compliance
Redwood Inference

---Reply---
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 11:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: ACME - endorsement language & COI timing

Thanks for the ping, Sofia. I reviewed the requested language and sketched a minimal-variance approach we can accept without escalated approvals. Key points below (and attached is a redline of the sample endorsement).

Summary of recommended ask to broker/insurer: 
- Naming: use the specific entity line: "ACME Technologies, Inc." (no blanket affiliates) plus the contract entity in the body of the order form. Avoid listing broad "subsidiaries and affiliates" unless ACME provides a schedule of entities.
- Endorsement form: insurer-issued endorsement preferred (CG 20 10 or equivalent with AI wording). If the insurer cannot issue an endorsement in time, we will accept a carrier-issued letter of confirmation that references policy number, endorsement text, and effective dates — but only as a temporary bridge. Insurer-signed endorsement required as final deliverable.
- Primary/Non-contrib: we will accept primary and non-contributory wording where the carrier expressly states that coverage is primary and non-contributing to any other insurance the Additional Insured may have. Wording example attached in redline.
- Waiver of subrogation: accept only if insurer confirms waiver applies to ACME relative to this contract (and only on property/damage lines as applicable).

Operational asks for the broker: 
1) Provide the insurer name, policy number, and expected delivery date for the endorsement/COI.
2) If delivering a carrier letter instead of endorsement, label it "Bridge confirmation - endorsement pending" and include a firm date when the insurer-signed endorsement will be issued.
3) Send endorsement PDF and COI to risk@redwood.com and attach the order form.

I've attached a redline (coa_v3_redline.docx) showing the precise clause and our preferred AI text. This should be shareable with the broker as the definitive spec. If they can get an insurer-issued endorsement matching it, we're good to accept. Otherwise we can accept the bridge confirmation with a deadline (no later than 30 days after countersignature).

Attachment: coa_v3_redline.docx (redline stub)

Kimberly Park
Legal Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

---Reply---
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 12:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: ACME - endorsement language & COI timing

Looping in operational acceptance: Risk team reviewed the redline and we can accept the bridge confirmation path only under these constraining conditions: 
- Bridge confirmation must include: insurer name, policy number, limits, effective/expiry dates, and explicit text that the insurer "will issue an endorsement naming ACME Technologies, Inc. as Additional Insured in form and substance substantially similar to the attached sample".
- Bridge confirmation must be received before countersignature; insurer-signed endorsement must be received within 14 calendar days post-countersignature. If the endorsement is not delivered within 14 days, we will trigger the fallback: temporarily suspend access to the ACME tenant until proof is provided (we will coordinate with Sales on suspension language).
- If ACME requires "subsidiaries and affiliates" named, we need a signed schedule of named entities from ACME attached to the COI.

I can approve the primary/non-contrib ask for this deal provided the insurer confirms in writing and it is insurer-signed.

Jonas Weber
Insurance Operations Lead
Redwood Inference

---Reply to External---
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@harborbrokers.com>, Contracts Team <contracts@acme.io>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 16:03:00 -0400
Subject: RE: ACME - endorsement language & COI timing

Evan / Maria — thanks for the quick follow. Per internal review (legal + risk):

What we need from the insurer / broker before we countersign:
- A COI showing current limits and policy number.
- A carrier-issued "bridge confirmation" letter (if endorsement cannot be issued before countersign) that includes insurer name, policy number, limits, effective/expiry dates, and an explicit commitment to issue an insurer-signed Additional Insured endorsement substantially similar to the attached sample. The bridge confirmation must be labeled: "Bridge confirmation - endorsement pending." 
- If the broker can get an insurer-issued endorsement (preferred), it should name exactly: "ACME Technologies, Inc." (no broad affiliates language) and include primary & non-contributory language if the insurer agrees.

Final deliverable schedule we can accept: 
- Bridge confirmation (or insurer endorsement) delivered prior to countersignature (we need the bridge confirmation before countersign to avoid delays).
- Insurer-signed endorsement to risk@redwood.com within 14 calendar days after countersignature.

Failure to provide an insurer-signed endorsement within 14 days will put us in a position where we may restrict access per our operational escalation (we'll coordinate with your contracts/sales to minimize disruption).

Please send the bridge confirmation or the insurer endorsement PDF to risk@redwood.com and cc contracts@redwood.com. If you expect delays, state the carrier name and policy number now so we can pre-approve the bridge confirmation content.

Attachments we expect: endorsement_sample_ACME.pdf (attached sample); orderform_signed_stub.pdf (we will attach when countersigned).

Let me know ETA — if you can get the bridge confirmation by EOD Thursday (2028-08-24) we'll be on track for countersign Friday.

Best,
Sofia
Senior Manager, Risk & Compliance
Redwood Inference

---End Thread---
